name: Security-Relevant System Properties
description: Reports explicit insecure property values and a non-standard adb_enabled setting, with non-assessment emulator and ADB posture telemetry.

evidenceUnits.title: Security-relevant property posture
evidenceUnits.observedObject: Selected Android security and debugging property values
evidenceUnits.proposition: An available property value matches an explicitly defined insecure rule
evidenceUnits.availability: Depends on property presence and successful property-service access
evidenceUnits.trustBoundary: User-space property APIs may be spoofed or hooked
evidenceUnits.inferenceLimit: An insecure value is contextual evidence and does not identify a root provider

evidenceUnits.title: Environment property posture
evidenceUnits.observedObject: Emulator and USB or ADB-related property values, and the Settings.Global adb_enabled value
evidenceUnits.proposition: adb_enabled holds a value outside {0, 1}, which neither the Settings UI nor AdbService writes; emulator and ADB-on posture is only described
evidenceUnits.observationChannel: Bionic system-property API and Settings.Global through the app ContentResolver
evidenceUnits.availability: Depends on property presence, successful property-service access, and a readable Settings.Global provider; from API 37 (Android 17 QPR1) the platform returns adb_enabled = 0 to third-party apps, so a 0 read there is recorded as redacted_by_platform and the rule is not evaluated
evidenceUnits.trustBoundary: User-space property APIs and in-process Settings reads may be spoofed or hooked, and the platform itself redacts adb_enabled for third-party apps from Android 17 QPR1
evidenceUnits.inferenceLimit: A non-standard adb_enabled value shows deliberate setting manipulation, not a root provider; a redacted_by_platform read is an unanswered channel, not ADB off, so the rule can fire only below API 37 or where the platform does not redact; emulator and ADB-on posture remain telemetry
